clue.text: Recital review may appear in the paper

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing a newspaper piece; the answer is the noun for what may appear there

indicators.note: to review is to go over again and recast, so the letters of the word before it are reworked

explanation.surface: A critic's write-up of a concert recital might be printed in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' reads as a newspaper notice of the recital, but it signals an anagram of RECITAL. The definition is descriptive: a newspaper piece is something that may appear in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is made up of written pieces, each one being an item that appears in print.

clue.text: Birds another turns to?

indicators.note: turns to here means the other bird's name, read backwards, becomes the answer

parts.note: another bird, a skua, a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: A question about which birds another bird turns into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for another bird, the SKUA, which reversed by 'turns to' gives the answer, itself a bird name.
explanation.definitionFit: These are diving seabirds of northern seas, such as the puffin and the guillemot.

clue.text: Little money at the end of the holiday

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word holiday

explanation.surface: A small sum of cash left over when the holiday is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives meaning very small in size.

clue.text: A cleaner fuel that draws well

definitions.meaning: a fuel that burns with less smoke than wood, used on barbecues
a stick of burnt wood used by artists for sketching

explanation.surface: A clean-burning fuel praised for having a good draught in the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws well' suggests a fire with a good draught; it really means an artist's sketching stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Charred wood is both a smokeless fuel and a soft black drawing medium.

clue.text: Make a run to clinch the match

definitions.text: Make a run to clinch the match

parts.words: Make a run to clinch the match
parts.note: reads like sport, a batsman scoring the winning run, but means a couple running away to secure their marriage

explanation.surface: A batsman scores the run that wins the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' and 'match' suggest cricket; the match is a marriage and the run is running off to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly to marry is to dash away and secure a wedding.

clue.text: Rabble's downfall

definitions.meaning: a contemptible bunch of people, as in British slang 'what a useless lot'
a fall of rain from the sky, a brief burst of rain

explanation.surface: The ruin of the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' looks like ruin but is literally rain falling down. 'shower' is British slang for a hopeless group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a useless group a shower, and a brief rainfall is also one.

clue.text: He's involved with any mistreated animals

indicators.note: mistreated suggests handled roughly, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters H, E and S

explanation.surface: A man is mixed up in cruelty to animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' scrambles HES (from He's) and ANY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are scavenging carnivorous mammals of Africa and Asia, so they are animals.

clue.text: Saw nothing unusual with this honest feller!

definitions.note: a person, the man in the cherry tree story who could not tell a lie

indicators.note: unusual suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A man admits he saw nothing odd, the very picture of honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' is both a fellow and one who fells trees: young George Washington supposedly confessed to chopping down a cherry tree, saying he could not tell a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: The first US president is famed in legend for honestly owning up to felling a cherry tree.

clue.text: Brutal advice to those who yield too easily

definitions.meaning: cruel and unremitting, showing no mercy

definitions.text: advice to those who yield too easily
definitions.meaning: a two-word instruction telling a soft touch to give in less often

explanation.surface: Harsh words for people who give way too readily.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into an instruction: relent less, that is, yield less often.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsparing and unremitting is harsh or brutal in its persistence.

clue.text: Jumper with a pocket

parts.note: sounds like a sweater with a pouch, but the jumper is a leaping marsupial carrying its young in a pouch

explanation.surface: A sweater that has a pocket on the front.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is a British word for a pullover sweater, which is the misleading picture; the real jumper is an Australian hopping animal with a pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: This marsupial moves by jumping and carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Creature featured in pop song

parts.note: an animal in the nursery rhyme whose title line is 'Pop goes the ...'

explanation.surface: An animal that appears in a chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop song' suggests chart music, but the song is the old nursery rhyme 'Pop Goes the Weasel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small carnivorous mammal that is the subject of an old song about popping.

clue.text: Threatened strikes that don't come off

definitions.text: Threatened strikes that don't come off

parts.words: Threatened strikes that don't come off
parts.note: sounds like industrial action that never happens, but means pretend blows in boxing or fencing

explanation.surface: Union walkouts that are threatened but never take place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests industrial action; here it means blows that are faked to mislead an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummy blows made to deceive an opponent are threatened attacks never carried through.

clue.text: Rate increase

parts.note: sounds like a rise in a tax or interest rate, but means a speeding up

explanation.surface: A rise in the rates or interest charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate increase' suggests a financial rise; in physics it is an increase in the rate of motion. Rates were a British local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, a rise in speed over time is exactly an increase of rate.

clue.text: Defeats come from fielding errors

definitions.meaning: brings down or topples, as of a government or ruler
in cricket, balls thrown in by fielders that go past the stumps, letting batsmen run extra

explanation.surface: Losses come from mistakes made in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a return throw that misses the stumps and lets the batsmen take extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a ruler is to defeat them, and wild throws in cricket share the name.

clue.text: Honest description of the company chairman's position

definitions.meaning: open and legitimate, without anything concealed

definitions.text: description of the company chairman's position
definitions.meaning: the chairman ranks over the board of directors

explanation.surface: An honest account of where the company chairman stands.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: the chairman sits above the board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealings done openly with nothing hidden are legitimate, and a chairman ranks over the board.

clue.text: About time Boris and Ivan developed common feelings

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so these letters are rearranged
developed suggests something worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Over time, two Russian men came to share the same feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' and 'developed' both signal the anagram of T (time), BORIS and IVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared emotional impressions or atmospheres are informally called vibes, short for this word.

clue.text: Northern blockhouses

parts.note: sounds like military forts, but means homes built of snow blocks in the Arctic

explanation.surface: Fortified buildings in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A blockhouse is a small fort; here the houses are literally made of blocks, of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit snow shelters are domed dwellings built from blocks of compacted snow in Arctic regions.

clue.text: Limb turned to solid jelly

indicators.note: turned suggests turning back, so the word for the limb is read backwards

explanation.surface: An arm or leg is turned into wobbly jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly-like semi-solid substance, as used in hair products, is this word.

clue.text: Vessel well protected from unusually cold rain

indicators.note: unusually suggests something out of the normal, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship keeps its crew dry from strangely cold rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges COLD and RAIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century warship clad with iron plating was a heavily protected vessel.

clue.text: Short clergyman to put his foot down for 12 across

definitions.meaning: the shortened title used for a Reverend

definitions.text: to put his foot down for 12 across
definitions.meaning: to press the accelerator to make an engine run faster

explanation.surface: A small vicar stamps his foot to speed things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put his foot down' looks like being firm; it means pressing the pedal to make the engine speed up, the 12 across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is abbreviated in writing, and racing an engine is a quick throttle burst.

clue.text: New schoolmasters lacking the places to teach

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters
lacking means the word the is taken out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Fresh teachers arrive without the rooms they need.
explanation.walkthrough: SCHOOLMASTERS less T, H and E leaves letters that 'New' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms in a school where lessons are given are the places for teaching.

clue.text: Declare at cricket match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match, played over up to five days

explanation.surface: Announce a declaration at a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declare' suggests a cricket captain closing an innings, but means to state formally.
explanation.definitionFit: To certify or affirm formally is to declare something true.

clue.text: Working as a tailor would appear to grow on one

definitions.text: Working as a tailor would appear to grow on one

parts.words: Working as a tailor would appear to grow on one
parts.note: a tailor might be making a garment such as a riding coat; the real sense is addictive

explanation.surface: A tailor's job seems to be getting more attractive to you.
explanation.walkthrough: A habit is also a garment, so a tailor is literally forming one; the real sense is something that becomes addictive, a habit that grows on you.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive tends to become ingrained through repetition, a usage that grows on you.

clue.text: Intends to make money

definitions.meaning: funds or resources, as in a person of independent wealth

explanation.surface: Plans to earn some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb to signify or intend, and the plural noun for one's financial resources.

clue.text: I'd see about the favourite

parts.note: taken as written, the letters I and D

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the word for see is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: I'll look into who the favourite is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is the old exclamation 'lo!', meaning look; 'about' turns it round. 'the' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is adored or hero-worshipped is a public favourite.

clue.text: Fight blows up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out with punches.
explanation.definitionFit: To box or argue without full force is to fight in a sparring way.

clue.text: Gave people your address

parts.note: sounds like handing out your home address, but means delivered a speech

explanation.surface: Told folk where you live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests where you live; it is a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering a formal speech to an audience is speaking publicly, giving them an address.

clue.text: Imagines being ordered into uniform

definitions.meaning: brings to mind, as a memory or image is summoned

explanation.surface: Someone daydreams about being conscripted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word joining the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Summoning an image to mind and being conscripted into the army share this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Teased about being placid

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm while being teased.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a calm, unhurried and composed temperament.

clue.text: He's no better, but puts something on a horse

definitions.text: He's no better, but puts something on a horse

parts.words: He's no better, but puts something on a horse
parts.note: sounds like a gambler placing a bet, but this tradesman fits a leather seat on the animal rather than a wager

explanation.surface: A man who doesn't gamble still puts something on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts something on a horse' suggests a bet; this craftsman makes the leather seat that goes on the horse's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of riding tack crafts the leather seats strapped onto horses.
